clue.text: Arsonist not quite stable, one wearing rubber

indicators.note: not quite means the word for stable loses its final letter

parts.note: stable means firm

indicators.note: one wearing rubber is dressed in it, so the rubber goes around one

parts.note: a rubber is an eraser
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An unstable person dressed in rubber turns out to be a firebug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one wearing rubber' pictures a person in a rubber suit; read cryptically, the eraser is worn around the numeral one, and 'not quite' clips the stable word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who deliberately starts fires is an arsonist.

clue.text: Old PM blowing top coming from Tel Aviv, perhaps

indicators.note: blowing top means the old prime minister's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister loses his temper on a visit from Tel Aviv.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like losing one's temper but means dropping the first letter of DISRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is a city in Israel, so a person from there is, for example, Israeli.

clue.text: Still ahead of time in competition

indicators.note: ahead of places the first piece before the second in this down entry

parts.note: still, as in 'still more', can mean even

explanation.surface: Someone is still ahead of the clock in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an event is a contest at a sports meeting.

clue.text: Supplement that may need to be removed?

definitions.meaning: an addition at the back of a book

definitions.text: that may need to be removed
definitions.meaning: the organ taken out by surgeons when inflamed

explanation.surface: An extra item that might have to be taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: matter added to the end of a book, and the small organ removed in an appendectomy.

clue.text: Plain sailing? Right on!

definitions.meaning: something simple and easy to deal with
directly ahead, as in going in a straight line onwards

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: uncomplicated and easy, and, split into two words, directly onwards.

clue.text: Distant meteor, rocky

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaken, so the letters of meteor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A far-off meteor made of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' looks like describing the meteor's material but signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something remote is far away.

clue.text: Second wager

definitions.meaning: to support or endorse, as a motion
to bet on, as a horse

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to support a proposal, and to put money on a horse.

clue.text: Book with complete chapter on winning flower

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense
up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A book with a whole chapter about a prize-winning bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a buttercup is a yellow wild flower.

clue.text: Solve first of conundrums humorist raised

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of conundrums is used

parts.note: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer of comic nonsense verse
raised means up

explanation.surface: A comic writer works out the first of some riddles that were put to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to clear up a mystery is to solve it.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland

parts.note: reads as the name of a Scottish bank, but means a hillside or slope in Scots

explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect word for a steep bank or hillside, beside a river for instance.

clue.text: System of betting in Lima, Peru — put off, losing plenty, initially

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the opening letter of plenty is the one taken

explanation.surface: A betting scheme in South America is cancelled for lack of interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' means the letters of LIMA PERU PUT, shuffled by 'off', lack the P that 'plenty, initially' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a pool betting system in which winners share the total stakes, as used on the tote.

clue.text: Church caretaker attacked carrying cross

indicators.note: carrying means the word for attacked holds the cross inside it

parts.note: set on means attacked
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A church caretaker was assaulted while holding a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sexton looks after a church and its graveyard.

clue.text: Elected Conservative must ring her right away on paper

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: must ring means the Tory surrounds the shortened her

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: right away means the R, for right, is removed from her

parts.note: taken as written before losing its R

explanation.surface: An elected Tory must phone her immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately', but here it means dropping R (right); 'must ring' is not a phone call but a surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: what works on paper is true in theory but not necessarily in practice.

clue.text: Shrink in car probing attractive person

indicators.note: probing means the car goes into the word for attractive person

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist in a car questions a good-looking person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist in the scene, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to diminish is to become smaller or reduce.

clue.text: Unconventional Irish soldier?

parts.note: a regular is a professional soldier of a standing army

explanation.surface: A guerrilla fighter from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as an irregular soldier, a guerrilla, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: irregular means not following convention or the rules.

clue.text: Manage to catch leader of expedition

parts.note: to cop is to catch, as police do

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of expedition

explanation.surface: Someone manages to capture the head of an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cope is to get by or handle things.

clue.text: Bird from USA crows jostled

indicators.note: jostled means pushed about, so the letters of USA crows are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird gets pushed around by American crows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the curassow is a large turkey-like bird of Central and South America.

clue.text: Leading performer, nearly bald

indicators.note: nearly means the word for bald loses its final letter

parts.note: stark means bare or bald, as in stark facts

explanation.surface: A top actor is going a bit bald.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the star is the lead performer in a show.

clue.text: Sporting call from friend in hot pants

indicators.note: in means the friend sits inside the rearranged letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of hot are muddled

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A shout at a sporting event from a pal wearing hot pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like clothing but is British slang for rubbish, signalling a jumble giving THO; 'in' places the friend inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cry fox hunters give when the quarry is sighted.

clue.text: Treacherous behaviour in crude piece of drama

parts.note: foul means crude or coarse
a play is a dramatic work

explanation.surface: Betrayal features in a vulgar stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: dishonest or criminal conduct, especially suspected murder.

clue.text: Reduce the length of a card game

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Shortening a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to abridge a text is to shorten it.

clue.text: End of play is baffling

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the close of a day's play when the umpires draw the wickets

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the cricket term for close of play, and a verb form meaning perplexes.

clue.text: Beggar beginning to board barge

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of board is used

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A tramp starts climbing aboard a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beggar' is the informal British term for a fellow, as in 'lucky beggar', not a mendicant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are informal British words for a person, often a rascal.

clue.text: Sounds like a sure-fire winner in state

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a cert is a racing term for a horse certain to win

explanation.surface: A tip for a guaranteed winner in a particular state.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to assert something is to declare it firmly.

clue.text: Silky material modelled at home

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the portrait
in means at home

explanation.surface: Smooth fabric worn by someone posing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' looks like an anagram signal for 'at', but it is the past tense sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: satin is a smooth, glossy woven fabric.

clue.text: Certainly, in every possible way

definitions.meaning: using all methods available, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a polite 'of course', and, read literally, through all possible methods.

clue.text: Fuss unduly, entertaining daughter

indicators.note: entertaining means the word for unduly holds the daughter inside

parts.note: too means excessively or unduly

explanation.surface: Making excessive commotion while hosting a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Swine in pub, drinking nothing

indicators.note: drinking means the pub takes in the nothing

parts.note: a bar is a pub
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pig in a pub, not having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boar is a male pig or wild swine.

clue.text: Team triumph, the German air-to-air missile

parts.note: a side is a team
to win is to triumph
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A team wins as a German missile scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Sidewinder is an American heat-seeking air-to-air missile.
